Alice M: Heads up — canary perf spike on model-x when continuous batching hits mixed kernel path. 99th went from 180ms -> 420ms after commit 3f9a.
Ben K: ugh, repro steps?
Alice M: repro is a burst of small seq requests (<=64) with occasional long seq (512) in same merging window. profiler snapshot pasted below.
Alice M: ```
# perf trace (sample)
kernel_select: path=A (small-optimized) -> B (vectorized-long) 3x switches
launch_ms: 0.9, 4.8, 0.95
memcpy_ms: 0.6
kv_lookup_ms: 0.2
token_ms_per_step: 2.2 -> 5.9
```
Carol S: looks like kernel swapping + launch overhead gets amortized badly when continuous batching mixes seq lengths. KV cache hits change effective seqlen distribution so selector flips mid-batch.
Dinesh: confirming — our selector currently picks per-batch using p50 seqlen. when a stray long request enters a mostly-short batch we flip kernels and rebind buffers, which costs ~3-6ms per switch.
Ben K: can we add a cooldown / sticky kernel to avoid thrash? e.g., prefer current kernel for N ms unless clear benefit. :thinking_face: 
Alice M: quick A/B showed sticky_window=100ms reduces 99p from 420 -> 220ms on canary for this workload. throughput unchanged.
perf-bot: [alert] regression_detected model-x canary 99p latency +130% — triggered 1759991300
Carol S: proposed autotune config snippet: 
```json
{"kernel_autotune": {"sticky_window_ms": 80, "seqlen_threshold_for_vector": 256, "swap_cost_estimate_ms": 4.0}}
```
Dinesh: also need to account for KV cache effect: when kv_cache_hit_ratio > 0.7 treat effective_seqlen = max(prefix_len, req_len) for selection, otherwise use observed batch distribution.
Ben K: test matrix to run: sticky {50,80,120} ms x seq_threshold {128,256,384} x kv_policy {on,off}. capture 50/90/99p + token cost.
Alice M: note: kernel B path has a memcpy-heavy codepath that spikes when batch_size < 8; that interacts poorly with sticky windows because it keeps smaller batches on the vectorized kernel. we need to either bias batching to fill or prefer small kernel for small batch counts.
Carol S: suggestion — try bucketing before merge: keep continuous batching but group by seqlen buckets (0-64,65-256,256+) and allow limited cross-bucket merge only if it reduces launch cost. tradeoff: slightly lower utilization vs lower tail.
Ben K: sounds good. action items: Alice -> run full canary matrix overnight + upload traces; Dinesh -> add memcpy counters and annotate kernel switch paths; Carol -> open PR for autotune defaults + add kv policy param; Ben -> schedule follow-up with perf owners.
Alice M: filing ticket INF-4021 with initial traces and canary notes: https://redwood/issue/INF-4021
Ben K: thanks all — lets sync on results tomorrow. :thumbsup:
